title: CreateModelVersion source-read check must authorize the proto-bound runId/modelId, not raw body keys
answers: authenticated user reads artifacts of a run they cannot access by creating a model version with runId
model version create skips the source run permission check when the body uses camelCase keys
basic-auth lets a registered model version point at a logged model or run without READ on it
CreateModelVersion camelCase alias bypasses the source READ check
body:
Symptom: a user with no READ on a run or logged model creates a model version from it, using a camelCase body key, and can then read that run's artifacts through their own registered model.
Root cause: mlflow/server/auth/__init__.py:validate_can_create_model_version checked raw Flask body keys `run_id` / `model_id`. The handler parses the body through the CreateModelVersion proto, which also binds `runId` / `modelId`, so the READ check was skipped for camelCase-only bodies.
Fix pattern: parse the body with `_get_request_message(CreateModelVersion())`, test presence with `msg.HasField(...)`, and authorize the bound value through `_get_run_permission` / `_get_model_permission` (via the `_can_read_model_version_source` helper). This is the same proto-first approach as validate_can_log_metric and validate_can_log_batch.
Constraints: HasField keeps the rule that an explicitly empty id is denied, not treated as absent. A non-dict body yields an empty message and falls through to handler validation. Tests should parametrize both the snake_case and camelCase spellings.
Applies: any basic-auth validator that anchors a new resource to a source run or model from the request body (model version create and similar routes).
applies: Authorization validators in mlflow/server/auth/__init__.py that read run_id or model_id from a request body.
says: Unauthorized users can access restricted run artifacts by creating a new registered model version.
Users without read permissions on an experiment run can link it to registered models.
Block users from creating model versions from runs they do not have permission to view.
Creating a model version bypasses read permission checks on the source experiment run.
Prevent unauthorized artifact access when registering a model version from another user's run.
search: In mlflow/server/auth/__init__.py:validate_can_create_model_version, authorization checks must validate protobuf-bound runId and modelId instead of inspecting raw Flask request body keys. Parsing request bodies with _get_request_message(CreateModelVersion()) and checking msg.HasField(...) prevents authorization bypasses when camelCase keys are submitted without read permissions on the source run or model. Bound identifiers are authorized using _get_run_permission and _get_model_permission via _can_read_model_version_source, ensuring explicitly empty identifiers are denied rather than treated as absent. This applies to basic-auth validators that anchor resources to source runs or models, and tests must cover both snake_case and camelCase forms.
